# Read-back

A wedding reception for 90 guests at Ashgrove Barn begins immediately after the 4pm ceremony ends. The event has three distinct phases: room setup and guest arrival (flip seating, dress tables, seat guests, welcome toast), food service (starters → mains → dessert across a single kitchen pass and two servers), and entertainment (first dance, speeches, cake cut, dancing until the band's final set). The sequence is tightly choreographed: the kitchen plates only one course at a time with no overlaps on the pass; the floor (two servers) serves and clears in lockstep with kitchen output; the MC controls all microphone moments (welcome, speeches, cake). The only slack is the canape window in the foyer, which absorbs photograph delays; everything downstream of the room call is fixed. Key constraints are one kitchen pass (the bottleneck; dessert will be held rather than plated early if speeches run long), one bar, one microphone, and two servers on the floor. The event must conclude by the band's last set. The planner controls the room call; the MC controls microphone cues and can flex speech timing within a 15–25 minute window.
